Query: For each customer, first order date, second order date (the min order_date greater than first). Then repeat = second - first ≤ 90. Join to customers for signup quarter. Group by cohort. Rate = count(repeat)/count(eligible).

Let me write SQL:
```
WITH fo AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_date
  FROM orders WHERE status NOT IN ('cancelled','returned')
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
so AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id, MIN(o.order_date) AS second_date
  FROM orders o JOIN fo ON fo.customer_id=o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status NOT IN ('cancelled','returned') AND o.order_date > fo.first_date
  GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT strftime('%Y', c.signup_date)||'-Q'||((CAST(strftime('%m',c.signup_date) AS INT)+2)/3) AS cohort,
  COUNT(*) AS eligible,
  SUM(CASE WHEN so.second_date IS NOT NULL AND julianday(so.second_date)-julianday(fo.first_date) <= 90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS repeats
FROM customers c
JOIN fo ON fo.customer_id=c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN so ON so.customer_id=c.customer_id
GROUP BY cohort ORDER BY cohort
```

title: Business intelligence
blurb: A sales analytics app over a live SQLite database: 1.0M orders, 2.1M order lines, 120K customers. The model explores the schema, runs SQL with the sandbox's ./sql tool and draws the dashboard as HTML with inline SVG.
